newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Canberra ends one-size-fits-all union deal.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Canberra ends one-size-fits-all union deal.

text.p: The Australian government said on Thursday it would ditch a single agreement which covers more than 130,000 federal public servants in about 100 agencies and departments in favour of individual or agency-based contracts.

"Individual agencies will be more accountable for improving their people management policies, their overall performance and, importantly, remuneration and other conditions of employment for public servants," Industrial Relations Minister Peter Reith said in a statement.

The Liberal-National conservative government began a review of the Australian Public Service (APS) late last year, saying that the bureaucratic system used to operate the APS restricted competition and productivity.

"Recent consultations with public servants on the reform of the APS revealed a pressing need to streamline public service processes, such as leave arrangements, promotion and appointment procedures and provide greater scope for improved pay and better performance management," Reith said.

But Reith said the government recognised differences between the public and private sectors and would address these in legislative changes to the Public Service Act and in its approach to agency-level agreement making.
The government also reviewed the practice of the Commonwealth deducting union dues, he said.
"Dues will only be collected with the written authority of members and provided the relevant union acts responsibly," he said.
The government has already moved to improve labour market efficiency.
Parliament passed the government's labour reforms last November, promising more jobs and faster economic growth.
It said the deregulation of the labour market would emphasise a freer market, reducing the role of unions which have traditionally supported the Labor Party which is now the key opposition group.
